text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Secondary school pupils and students demonstrated in front of government buildings against new law on minority languages at the pedagogical faculty in Skopje. They demanded resignation of Education Minister Sofija Todorova.
- Macedonian Deputy Prime Minister Jane Miljovski is in Germany to meet Finance Ministry officials and ask for German support for Macedonia at the Bosnia Donors conference on February 25 in Brussels.
- Macedonian Education Minister Sofija Todorova said there was no reason for her resignation, the new law on minority languages had been adopted by parliament and would be enacted.
- Prime Miniter Branko Crvenkovski received representatives of railway workers trade unions, who are demanding regular salaries and better working conditions.
- Several senior members of the democratic party said they are against assimilating their party with the Liberal Party.
